status: PREPARED — the Product Owner's ASR recording simplification (2026-10-28): Speechmatics Enhanced ar_en only, real-time streaming over WebSocket, on the Product Owner's own 20 phone recordings; one bounded run after an explicit approval (asr-sm-approval.json). Nothing has been sent.
supersedes: plan version 1 (sha256 e6b233b62675ca18009cc14ddef693afee1478bc14f2e92d188b8286e44379be: 120 sessions, 2 speakers, Enhanced ar_en + Melia 1, USD 1), SUPERSEDED by the Product Owner, never approved and never run; its approval record is not reused

scope.note: One speaker (the Product Owner), 20 recordings, one phone. The results are a preliminary single-speaker test: they do not show how Speechmatics performs for other speakers, voices, phones or rooms, and they are never reported as such.

region: EU (pinned; the global endpoint may route anywhere)

guard.keyFile: ~/.qandeel/speechmatics-api-key.txt (per user, outside the repository; read into memory by the launcher only)
guard.reservation: each session reserves its timeout (the recording's audio + the tail silence + the margin) at the arm's hourly price, and settles at its measured wall time, which bounds the audio Speechmatics can bill

terms.holds: real-time audio is never recorded or stored; it is processed in memory and the transcripts are returned and discarded
clause 10.4: no use of customer data for machine learning or model training unless the workspace opts in (the portal model-training setting)
the model-training opt-in (a 33 % discount) is off by default

settings: the workspace model-training setting stays OFF; the Product Owner confirms it in the approval (modelTrainingOff: true) before the run
real-time only: no batch job is created, so nothing is held for the batch retention of 7 days
no translation, no speaker identification, no audio events
privacy.notes: The Product Owner's recordings, their converted WAVs and the transcripts stay in gitignored directories and are deleted at S8B-01 closure.

arms.role: the only arm (Product Owner): the Speechmatics configuration with Arabic–English code-switching in one stream, server end-of-utterance detection, max_delay control and a custom dictionary

audio.encoding: pcm_s16le, the WAV's own sample rate (mono; channels averaged)
audio.format: the phone's own format; asr-sm.mjs --prepare converts it locally to 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV with convert-audio.ps1 (Windows Media Foundation; nothing installed, nothing sent); a streamable WAV is used as it is

set.name: po20
set.speakerNote: PO: the Product Owner, recording their own voice on their own phone
set.recordings: artifacts/evals/s8b-01/corpus/PO/NN.<phone format> (01 … 20), converted to PO/wav/NN.wav with PO/wav/prepared.json binding source and WAV hashes (gitignored)

measures: WER / CER, corpus level, per dialect, category and condition; English words scored in Latin or a listed Arabic spelling
checks: names / key terms, numbers (digits or the spoken words), the intended word of a self-correction, the English words
first partial after speech onset; the last final after speech end; E = EndOfUtterance after speech end; A = the last final after EndOfUtterance; final lag after its audio

acceptance.note: Preregistered for ENHANCED_AR_EN. From bench-plan.json asr.proposedThresholds (WER, A) and the plan's 0.5 s end-of-utterance trigger, unchanged from plan version 1. The recommendation follows them; the decision is the Product Owner's. 20 recordings of one speaker (18 Egyptian: 15 on the speaker phone, 2 in noise, 1 with QANDEEL's voice playing; 2 MSA) are a preliminary single-speaker test: a small group's rate is read with that caution, and nothing is claimed for all users.
